required_justification: Proof that the admission is a planned inpatient hospitalization (suraksha_gold_policy#6)
Confirmation that pre‑authorisation is mandatory for planned inpatient stays irrespective of cost (suraksha_gold_policy#6)
Evidence that the cardiac condition is not a pre‑existing disease under the policy definition (suraksha_gold_policy#5)
Documentation that the insurer bears the burden of proof for any PED exclusion (claims_procedure_and_grievance#6)
clinical_justification: Violet Belinda Rosenbaum, a 66‑year‑old female with a documented history of coronary artery bypass grafting, was admitted for inpatient cardiac care. In patients with prior CABG, ongoing monitoring, medication optimisation and discharge planning are essential to prevent recurrent ischemic events, as the standard of care for acute coronary syndromes includes ECG, cardiac biomarkers and angiographic assessment (acute_coronary_syndrome#3). The inpatient stay enables completion of required investigations and ensures a safe transition to home, fulfilling the medical necessity for continued cardiac management. Accordingly, the discharge request is part of a planned inpatient episode that meets the policy’s pre‑authorisation criteria.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
citations.quote:
## 3. Pre-Authorisation  
### 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
Prior authorisation is mandatory for (a) every planned In-patient Hospitalisation and (b) any treatment with an estimated cost above ₹50,000.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
citations.quote:
### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. A condition first diagnosed ON OR AFTER the policy start date is NOT a Pre-Existing Dise

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Acute Myocardial Infarction — Emergency Revascularisation > Medical Necessity
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity
Diagnosis is supported by ischaemic symptoms, ECG changes and raised troponin. Coronary angiography followed by PCI with stenting is the standard of care for STEMI and high-risk NSTEMI.

citations.section: Acute Myocardial Infarction — Emergency Revascularisation > Documentation
citations.quote:
## Documentation
ECG tracings, troponin values, the angiography report, the stent details and the discharge summary.
